purpose: Canonical scope-classification cases shared by three implementations of one rule: the designer's classifyPrimitive (TypeScript), app.primitives_search_store.classify_scope (Python) and SCOPE_EXPRESSION (SQL). A copy of this file lives at private-suite/designer/tests/fixtures/primitive-scope-cases.json; the two must be edited together, and each side's test asserts this revision number so a one-sided edit fails loudly.

cases.why: The JSON Schema base types: a system row filed under a .../primitives namespace.
A trailing slash is not part of the namespace; both sides strip it before matching.
Several trailing slashes strip the same way (the client uses /\/+$/, not a single cut).
The separator is required: a namespace merely named 'primitives' is not a .../primitives one.
The word must end the namespace, not merely appear in it.
A leading-slash namespace still ends with /primitives.
The derived and composite system types.
A namespace-less system row is Core, never Standard — the client's `p.namespace &&` guard.
An empty namespace is falsy on the client and empty in SQL; both land on Core.
A namespace of nothing but slashes reduces to empty, so it is Core.
An imported *system* row is still classified by namespace: provenance only splits tenant rows.
A tenant row authored in the app.
A tenant row is Tenant whatever its namespace looks like — .../primitives does not promote it.
A tenant row that arrived through an import is Custom.
Provenance is matched exactly: only the literal 'imported' is Custom.
A legacy flat primitive with no namespace is a plain tenant type.
